reach-seams-c (c) HANDED TO P, 3 events, the OVER cursor arm: fn-nntp-over-range-ovw-expands-to-over-range-cat, fn-nntp-over-range-ovw-emits-a-fresh-cursor, fn-ovw-run-of-start-is-cursor-octets (PRF-1020). FINDING: the running dispatcher answers OVER/XOVER ranges with fn-nntp-over-range-indexed (host chain: fn-nntp-archive-pinned-arms -> fn-nntp-over-range-indexed, books/nntp-range-indexed.lisp: the whole reply as materialized lines). Nothing reached calls fn-nntp-over-range-ovw or fn-ovw-start (the cat arms fn-nntp-archive-command-cat and fn-nntp-xref-reply-cat are unreached), so the OVER cursor quantum host/native/owner.lisp documents as bounding an OVER hold (fnn-owner-over-window) only ever sees NEWNEWS and LIST cursors. This is a feature the host prose claims and the dispatcher does not wire, not a naming gap. P decides: wire fn-nntp-over-range-ovw into the pinned dispatch (a host/books change with a dispatch equality), or re-scope PRF-1020's OVER claims to the reader the node runs.

No host line reaches any fn-owb-* transition (books/owner-batch.lisp header: 'until it lands no host line calls this book'); the host's commit quantum runs the concrete kernel fn-lgc-* (fn-olr-take refinement, fn-lgu-acknowledge) and the crash-image subjects here (fn-bs-crash, fn-bs-durable-content, fn-bs-fsync-file, fn-lg-scan, fn-lg-prefixp) are the byte-store crash model and the reference scan, which the host realizes with the OS and the streaming fn-lgw-step-buf loop (fn-lgw-run, the whole-segment equivalent, is unreached: the loop is Lisp, so no ACL2 function equals it). No equality of the checker's shape exists to name. P: either restate T1/T4/T7 over the entries the host calls (fn-lgc-*, fn-lgu-*; books/store-log-durable.lisp already carries M1 at fnn-log-finish) or declare them campaign-tied crash-model claims judged by tests/campaign (native_cuts LOG_CUTS fn-lg-append-program / fn-lg-fence-program).

(ii) fn-zpl-pool-check-is-pool-okp and fn-zpl-pool-okp-of-nil (PRF-949): books/deflate-pool-check.lisp states 'no served path calls the check'; the first equates a test twin to the invariant, the second is the invariant's base case; both are about fn-zpl-pool-okp, a spec predicate fn-zpl-decode-bufs re-establishes, which no host line evaluates; re-scope as test/diagnosis evidence. (iii) fn-oclc-ready-cst-relation-is-history-relation (PRF-274): a premise-discharge fact about fn-cpo-history-relation; the host's fn-oclc-configure is the carried form that replaced the fn-cpo-configure-durable replay and never evaluates the relation, so there is no host line to name; record as a proof-side premise, not a served claim. (iv) fn-olr-take-never-joins-the-batch-in-flight (PRF-288): the host runs fn-lgc-take, related to fn-olr-take by fn-lgc-take-refines, a three-way conjunction over the abstraction fn-lgc-of that reach_check's equality/square shapes do not read; a single accepted-shape square would need an abstraction function polymorphic over a state and a take answer, which I did not invent. A checker teaching of conjunctive refinements, or a restatement of the claim over fn-lgc-take, is P's. (v) fn-store-prepare-interned-keeps-the-stored-octets (PRF-180): the host runs fn-psrv-store-prepare-next then a separate fn-arena-seal-list in another process (fn-store-prepare-interned-carried-is-next-then-seal is an mv-valued equality to fn-store-prepare-interned-carried, itself unreached); no single reached function equals fn-store-prepare-interned, so (a) would need the host to call the carried entry once across the store-node/io split.
